drafted_from: tool:retire-a-servers-old-builds's row in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/tool-rows.json, do-work/renew-a-tls-certificate.mjs, do-work/tls-host-owner.py and the tests in test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Retire the old hand-road build folders on my server at 192.0.2.34, but keep the one the seed runs from." It runs tool:retire-a-servers-old-builds and says how many it removed.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it takes one server's facts as its input and answers what that server's certificate owner reports.
instructions: 1. Gather the server's facts: its public name, IPv4 address, SSH port, the administrator you sign in as, its pinned key ("<address> ssh-ed25519 <key>") and its layout (host: owner path, state folder, downloads folder, ingress, receptionist). The README in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/ shows a made-up one.

2. Say to your AI the sentence in start_here. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:retire-a-servers-old-builds and that input (the worked example shows one). The door mounts your server administration key for the run; you paste no key.
3. Read what comes back: {"retired": <how many folders were removed>}. An {"error": ...} or a thrown message names what to change (for example the layout or the pinned key was refused).
4. host.receptionist.releases.retire ({folder, name}) is required; only real folders whose whole name matches `name` go, and never the one the receptionist is held on.

worked_examples.title: Remove two of three old builds
worked_examples.given: From tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/test/tls-host-owner.test.py (retiring the hand road): under /opt/example/source sit folders named a x40, b x40 and not-a-build; the seed runs from the b folder, so only the a folder is removed.
